text:
Claire (product): Quick sync — embeddings API priority for Q2. We need to lock batching limits, default dimension, model defaults (hosted + dedicated), and the response envelope before Friday's roadmap review.

Devin (eng-platform): Can we separate 'bulk' vs 'single' paths? Customers want both low-latency single embeds and high-throughput bulk. Need concrete numbers to pick defaults.

Sam (eng-ml): For model choices: redwood-emb-small (512d), redwood-emb-medium (1024d), redwood-emb-large (1536d). Tradeoffs: small is cheaper, large gives recall gains. Suggest default=1024 for hosted, 1536 allowed for Dedicated with explicit cost warning.

Meera (solutions): Big customer ask from Acme Health: they need batch up to 512 IDs in one request for ingestion pipelines. They expect server-side batching to be supported.

Devin (eng-platform): 512 requests in one HTTP call is fine, but we need to gate by payload size and downstream GPU memory. proposal: max_batch_limit=512 overall, per-instance streaming window=128 to avoid OOM; platform shards large requests internally.

Claire (product): Launch must-haves: 1) API shape stable (no breaking changes) 2) default model decided 3) latency SLOs for single embed and batch 4) docs + SDK examples

Sam (eng-ml): Suggested SLOs: single embed (batch=1) p95 <= 60ms hosted-small, <=40ms dedicated; bulk throughput measured as embeds/sec: e.g., batch=64 1536d on a T4x8 equiv -> ~150 embeds/sec.

AJ (cs): Acme Health will only sign if we support per-item metadata passthrough and per-request id mapping. Also they want deterministic seed option for reindexing.

Meera (solutions): Put these in API: allow "ids": [..] and return parallel "ids": [..] in response. Also "metadata_flat" passthrough field.

Devin (eng-platform): Draft request/response (suggested):

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model":"redwood-emb-medium",
  "input":["doc1","doc2"],
  "ids":["row-1","row-2"],
  "include_metadata":true,
  "compress":"none"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "object":"list",
  "model":"redwood-emb-medium-2026-02",
  "ids":["row-1","row-2"],
  "data":[
    {"id":"row-1","embedding":[0.001, -0.002, ...], "metadata":{"source":"acme"}},
    {"id":"row-2","embedding":[...], "metadata":{}}
  ]
}
```

Sam (eng-ml): One optimization: support a compressed base64 embedding payload for bulk responses to reduce bandwidth, opt-in via "compress":"zstd_base64". Need to ensure SDKs transparently decode.

Devin (eng-platform): Implementation constraints: 1) enforce per-request payload byte limit (e.g., 10MB uncompressed) 2) enforce max_batch_limit=512 3) internal slice size=128 so we process in sub-batches 4) impose per-embedding dimension whitelist [512,1024,1536]

Claire (product): Prioritization: Must-have for GA: model default=1024, public request/response shape w/ ids+metadata, max_batch_limit=512, SDK examples, docs, basic zstd compression opt-in. Nice-to-have: server-side dedupe, streaming embed responses, auto-quantized variants.

AJ (cs): Will present this to Acme tomorrow. If GA supports their flow, we can close the deal. Please flag any blocker ASAP.

deploy-bot: Note: upcoming breaking-change window closes in 72 hours. Coordinate rollout with platform team.

Devin (eng-platform): I'll open an RFC with perf numbers and a prototype PR by EOD. Sam, can you run microbenchmarks for batch sizes [1,8,64,128] across dims?

Sam (eng-ml): On it. I'll share numbers in the RFC. Early note: 1536 dims multiply memory and network costs noticeably — we should publish cost multipliers.

Claire (product): Thanks everyone. Action items: Devin RFC + PR, Sam perf numbers, Meera sample request for Acme, AJ to confirm contract terms conditional on these specs. Back on this thread after RFC lands.
